edits.original: Blessed is the one who doesn't walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of scoffers;

edits.original: Don't remember the sins of my youth, nor my transgressions. Remember me according to your loving kindness, for your goodness' sake, YHWH.

edits.original: Consider my affliction and my travail. Forgive all my sins.

edits.rationale: Hebrew poetry/wisdom: preserve figurative images and address culpability without permanent human labels.

edits.original: Don't gather my soul with sinners, nor my life with bloodthirsty men;

edits.original: I acknowledged my moral failure to you. I didn't hide my iniquity. I said, I will confess my transgressions to YHWH, and you forgave the iniquity of my sin. Selah.

edits.original: For they flatter themselves in their own eyes, too much to detect and hate their sin.

edits.original: There is no soundness in my flesh because of your indignation, neither is there any health in my bones because of my sin.

edits.original: I said, "I will watch my ways, so that I don't sin with my tongue. I will keep my mouth with a bridle while the wicked is before me."

edits.original: I said, "YHWH, have mercy on me! Heal me, for I have sinned against you."

edits.original: Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity. Cleanse me from my sin.

edits.rationale: Hebrew poetry/wisdom: preserve figurative images and address culpability without permanent human labels.

edits.original: Against you, and you only, have I sinned, and done that which is broken in your sight; that you may be proved right when you speak, and justified when you judge.

edits.original: Hide your face from my sins, and blot out all of my iniquities.
edits.final: Hide your face from my moral failures, and blot out all of my iniquities.
edits.rationale: Hebrew poetry/wisdom: preserve figurative images and address culpability without permanent human labels.

edits.original: Then I will teach transgressors your ways. Sinners shall be converted to you.

edits.original: For, behold, they lie in wait for my soul. The mighty gather themselves together against me, not for my disobedience, nor for my sin, YHWH.

edits.original: All things come alike to all. There is one event to the righteous and to the wicked; to the good, to the clean, to the unclean, to the one who sacrifices, and to the one who doesn't sacrifice. As is the good, so is the sinner; the one who takes an oath, as the one who fears an oath.

edits.original: Wisdom is better than weapons of war; but one sinner destroys much good.
